elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Company

elements.element: Customer consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: and in no event to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: no change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Insertion grants Customer-side free assignment only; no notice mechanic and Vendor assignment requires consent

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)

reasons: All atomic preferred elements are present in the inserted operative language: Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment gated by Customer consent not unreasonably withheld, absolute competitor bar, and express denial of any Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
The locked target level (preferred) is fully satisfied; the fallback's mutual-notice mechanic is intentionally not adopted and need not be, since preferred and fallback are separate bargains.
Minimal: a single concise insertion after the bare successors-and-assigns sentence, with no rewrite of the original sentence, no new exceptions, and no surplus boilerplate.
Preserves intent: original binding-on-successors language remains effective; defined terms 'Company' and 'HDI' are used consistently and no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.
